title: Why Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) Stock Is Tied to Nvidia’s CEO Shake-Up - Blockonomi
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) stock fell 5.7% to 2,215 in Taiwan trading on Monday. Asian chip names took a beating all day. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited, TSM Taiwan’s Taiex lost 2,635 points, or 6.03%, and closed at 41,040. That was the second-largest closing point drop in the index’s history. The U.S.-listed ADRs had not opened yet when the Asian session ended. So the 5.7% figure covers Taiwan trading only. Foxconn fell harder, down about 9.3%, according to The Wall Street Journal. South Korea’s Kospi and Japan’s Nikkei slid too. The Associated Press had the Kospi down about 3.6% and the Nikkei down about 2.4%. Another tally put the Kospi near 4%, which comes down to timing. On November 12, Nvidia (NVDA) said Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO. CFO Colette Kress is now interim chief. Nvidia was not the only worry. Weak Chinese economic data and a contraction in Japan’s economy also hurt sentiment. Questions about AI valuations and long-term returns were already in the air. The CEO news landed right on top of them. TSMC builds the vast majority of Nvidia’s AI accelerator chips. So doubts about Nvidia’s direction can quickly turn into doubts about TSMC’s order book. AMD is another TSMC customer, with chips that run AI servers and data centers. Nvidia stock was down about 2% in the latest quote. A falling stock price does not mean orders were canceled. The selloff reflects trading, not a company update. Nvidia reports fiscal third-quarter results Tuesday, November 17, after the U.S. close. Analysts expect revenue of about $109 billion and earnings growth of 90%. The company had guided for revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%. Those are forecasts, not reported results. Investors will look at data center demand, profit margins and the AI spending outlook. Guidance on accelerator demand is the line to find. Anthropic’s IPO is also set for this week. Together with Nvidia’s report, it will test whether the AI rally has more room to run. Monday’s U.S. session will show whether the Asian weakness spreads to American-listed chip stocks. Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited TSM is adding outside manufacturing support to one of the most constrained parts of its artificial intelligence supply chain. A five-year, $2 billion agreement with GlobalFoundries Inc. GFS will establish another source of silicon interposers for TSM's CoWoS advanced-packaging ecosystem.That matters because back-end capacity remains constrained even as AI-related demand expands. Packaging availability can limit how quickly wafer demand becomes finished product revenue, making added interposer supply strategically important. GlobalFoundries plans to manufacture silicon interposers at its Malta, NY, facility, with volume production expected to begin ramping in the first half of 2028. The agreement gives TSM a U.S.-based source for a component used in advanced packages and provides a framework for future capacity expansion.The arrangement also broadens TSM's manufacturing support beyond its own facilities. GlobalFoundries said the program is designed to expand capacity over time as customer demand grows, giving the partnership room to scale beyond the initial commitment. CoWoS sits within TSM's broader 3DFabric portfolio, which combines chip stacking and advanced packaging technologies to connect logic, memory and other components. That integration is increasingly important as customers build larger computing systems that require more components to work together efficiently.Additional interposer supply could eventually help TSM support customers moving toward larger and more complex AI packages. Management said CoWoS remains the leading choice for customers and noted that TSM is already producing packages at five times reticle size while developing larger formats. The deal does not solve the current bottleneck. Qualification work and production execution still need to occur before the planned 2028 volume ramp, leaving near-term back-end constraints in place.TSM has acknowledged a shortage in back-end supply and said demand remains above its current ability to supply. Until outside capacity arrives, revenue conversion will continue to depend on internal expansion, tool conversions, productivity gains and better capacity utilization. Outside manufacturing support adds flexibility to TSM's broader capacity strategy. Rather than relying on a single source for every packaging component, the company can combine internal expansion with specialized external supply when that helps customers secure enough front-end and back-end capacity.That approach fits management's wider planning process, which includes checking data-center construction and electricity availability as well as component supply. Amkor Technology, Inc. AMKR is pursuing a similar industry opportunity by expanding its Arizona advanced-packaging and test campus, with planned investment rising to about $12 billion as customer commitments increase. The GlobalFoundries agreement strengthens the long-term packaging capacity story, but execution remains central. The benefit depends on successful qualification, a timely 2028 ramp and TSM's ability to coordinate wafer output, packaging availability and customer infrastructure readiness.TSM currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). Its Growth Score of B supports the earnings and AI-demand case, while the Value Score of D, Momentum Score of F and VGM Score of D call for greater selectivity. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited TSM continues to benefit from accelerating artificial intelligence demand, leading-edge process adoption and rising earnings. Third-quarter 2026 revenues increased 41.2% year over year in U.S. dollar terms, while earnings per American depositary receipt climbed 57.5%.The growth case is substantial, but so is the investment burden. Higher capital spending, overseas manufacturing costs and a valuation that is not uniformly inexpensive make the stock less straightforward to chase after its strong growth. High-performance computing accounted for 68% of third-quarter 2026 revenues and grew 22% sequentially. Management raised its 2026 U.S. dollar revenue growth outlook to around 44%, up from slightly above 40% in July, as demand for differentiated technologies and a broader customer base remained favorable.Two-nanometer technology contributed 8% of wafer revenues, up from 3% in the prior quarter. That rapid adoption reinforces TSM's leading-edge growth profile and supports higher-value manufacturing demand as artificial intelligence workloads expand. TSM trades at 18.0X forward 12-month earnings, below the 18.8X multiple for its industry. On that measure alone, the shares do not look stretched relative to peers.The broader valuation picture is less forgiving. Price-to-book, price-to-cash-flow and price-to-sales ratios remain materially above industry levels, which helps explain the stock's Value Score of D. The earnings multiple discount therefore does not make TSM uniformly inexpensive. TSM retained a 2026 capital budget of $60 billion-$64 billion and expects investment during 2026-2028 to substantially exceed the preceding three-year period. That spending is needed to expand advanced-node and packaging capacity, including the N2 family, whose annual capacity is expected to more than double in 2027.Cash generation provides support. Operating cash flow totaled $75.67 billion in the first nine months of 2026, although property, plant and equipment purchases reached $40.64 billion. The same AI investment cycle is benefiting equipment supplier Applied Materials, Inc. AMAT, which reported 22% fiscal 2026 growth in Semiconductor Systems revenues. Geographic diversification comes with a margin cost. Overseas fabs are expected to dilute full-year 2026 gross margin by roughly two percentage points, with management still expecting three to four points of dilution later in the multiyear expansion cycle.The N2 ramp is adding near-term pressure as well. Gross margin fell 1.3 percentage points sequentially to 66.4% in the third quarter, primarily because of initial N2 costs, even as revenues rose sharply. GlobalFoundries Inc. (GFS) adds another piece to the capacity strategy through a multiyear agreement to supply silicon interposers for advanced packaging, with production expected to begin ramping in 2028. TSM still has a favorable near-term setup, but the case favors selective buying rather than an aggressive valuation-driven entry. Artificial intelligence demand, leading-edge adoption and earnings growth remain supportive, while capital intensity and overseas costs raise the execution bar.The stock currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). Its Growth Score of B fits the earnings and demand profile, but the Value Score of D, Momentum Score of F and VGM Score of D are less supportive.
